titleEn: Tails Have Their Way, Legs Have Theirs!

pages.text: "I want to climb, too!" Mumu reached for a low branch of the stream tree. Taro already sat on it, his long tail dangling. Mumu's hands slipped off.
"I want to climb like Taro." Mumu bounded up and tried hanging again, but slipped. "Taro has a tail, and I don't."
Mumu plopped down under the tree, ears drooping forward. "Long legs aren't useful for anything."
Taro jumped down. "Look over there." He pointed to a ripe fruit dangling at a branch's tip.
Taro climbed again, wrapped his tail around the branch, and reached out. But the branch swayed; he could go no farther. "I can't reach! It will break if I go farther."
Mumu turned their ears. "Wait, chickens are coming." Their feet pattered from the road's end. "If the fruit falls, the chickens will eat it first!"
Mumu pushed with their hind legs and bounded high. One hand plucked the fruit from the branch's tip. Taro clapped. "Tails Have Their Way, Legs Have Theirs!"
"My legs are useful, too!" Mumu bounded once more on the spot. They sat under the tree and shared the fruit in halves.
Now they picked fruit together. Taro wrapped his tail around a branch and shook it; Mumu bounded with long legs to catch the fruit. "Tails Have Their Way, Legs Have Theirs!"

They gently touched foreheads. "Your legs are wonderful." Being different was no reason for envy. Each had something different that was long. Mumu bounded away. "Tails Have Their Way, Legs Have Theirs!"
